lead.headline: Nepal flood toll passes 470 as a barrier lake threatens new deluge
lead.dek: More than 1,500 are missing across Nepal and Tibet, and a blocked river is swelling above the disaster zone
body: Nepal's prime minister's office said Friday that 469 people are confirmed dead and 977 missing, two days after a glacier collapse sent a wall of ice, rock and mud down Himalayan river valleys and buried whole villages. Chinese authorities count three dead and 558 missing across the border in Tibet, where 260 of the missing are foreign nationals.

Attention is now on an unstable barrier lake at the Nepal-China border, formed where flood debris dammed a river. Chinese authorities say it holds about 2 million cubic meters of water, with 3 million more expected within three days; a burst would send a second flood down valleys where roughly 42 kilometers of road are already gone. About 1,550 people have been rescued, 800 of them by helicopter, and Nepal has deployed 30,000 security personnel.

Nepal says 644 of its missing are foreigners, and NPR reported about 90 Americans remain unaccounted for, with no American deaths confirmed by the State Department as of Thursday. Kathmandu says it does not need international search teams; the U.S. has pledged $500,000 and the U.N. $2.5 million, and India has sent helicopters with supplies.

briefs.headline: Cook rebuffs Trump's second attempt to fire her from the Fed
briefs.summary: The Fed governor's lawyers answered the White House's fraud allegation with "an inadvertent error is not fraud," noting Trump and cabinet members face similar mortgage claims; a June 5-4 ruling shields governors from at-will removal.

briefs.headline: ICE arrests of people without criminal records hit a record
briefs.summary: New federal data show ICE averaged more than 800 arrests a day of people with no criminal record in July — over half of all arrests for the first time — as the White House pushes toward 2,000 a day.

briefs.headline: Artemis II crew receives top space honor in Houston today
briefs.summary: Trump presents the Congressional Space Medal of Honor to Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen at 11 a.m. ET at Johnson Space Center; the four flew Orion around the Moon in April.

briefs.headline: Education Department opens accreditation overhaul to comment
briefs.summary: The proposed rule, published Aug. 20, would ease the path for new college accreditors, bar standards requiring racial preferences and add intellectual-diversity duties; comments run through Sept. 21.

briefs.headline: Norway's King Harald V dies at 89 after 35 years on the throne
briefs.summary: The king died peacefully at Oslo University Hospital early Friday after an August hospitalization for a blood infection; Crown Prince Haakon, 53, succeeds him. He had reigned since 1991.

briefs.headline: Haiti police pressed for answers on Kenscoff massacre
briefs.summary: At a brief Thursday news conference, a police spokesman declined to discuss any plan for the more than 50 hostages taken in Sunday's attack that killed 47; the U.N. migration agency counts 2,600 displaced.

briefs.headline: Qatar's premier presses Hormuz reopening on Tehran visit
briefs.summary: Sheikh Mohammed met Foreign Minister Araghchi on Thursday — the first high-level Qatari visit since the war began — pushing a phased corridor and mine-clearing plan; Hormuz oil flows have fallen from 20 million barrels a day to 5 million.

briefs.headline: Zambia questions election runner-up over alleged treason
briefs.summary: Police recorded "warn and caution" statements from opposition leader Brian Mundubile and his running mate after Mundubile surrendered Thursday, two weeks after a raid on his home in which a former minister was shot dead.

briefs.headline: Anthropic to pay $45B for computing at Mason County campus
briefs.summary: Bloomberg reported Thursday the AI firm will rent about a third of Nscale's Monarch Compute Campus north of Point Pleasant for six years — some 460 megawatts. Morrisey called it "an extraordinary vote of confidence"; Nscale declined comment.

briefs.headline: Justice and Morrisey trade jabs over the Greenbrier's new owner
briefs.summary: After the Lottery Commission approved the resort's casino license under Kennedy Lewis control, Morrisey welcomed "much needed financial stability"; Justice answered that he'd "keep building," and Morrisey blamed his "financial mismanagement."

briefs.headline: Court tosses ethics case over judge's foster care remarks
briefs.summary: The state Supreme Court on Wednesday dismissed the disciplinary case against Kanawha Circuit Judge Maryclaire Akers, brought over a 2025 radio interview on children housed in hotels; a hearing board had found insufficient evidence.

regional.item: Yeager Airport is tallying lightning and water damage from the Aug. 16 storm to its electrical and security systems for an insurance claim.
A Richwood man was charged with murder after a dispute between neighbors in Holcomb turned fatal Wednesday evening, state police said.

away.item: Vandals sprayed slurs on the Vermont Veterans Home's honor-roll monuments last Saturday; veterans and volunteers cleaned them within hours.

hotspots.item: Surf City is seeking engineering proposals for parking upgrades at the Goldsboro Avenue public lot, posted Aug. 18 with proposals due Sept. 22.

briefs.headline: Lheidli T'enneh opens the Ancient Forest interpretive centre
briefs.summary: The First Nation held a soft opening Thursday for the Chun T'oh Whudujut centre on Highway 16, built with $7.8 million in federal and provincial funding and 1,800 volunteer hours; the full opening is set for May 2027.

briefs.headline: B.C. lifts its wildfire state of emergency two days early
briefs.summary: The province ended the Aug. 8 declaration Thursday on emergency officials' advice, saying the powers were never needed; evacuation orders and alerts remain in place and fire risk stays elevated in the dry Interior.

briefs.headline: Quebec opens a 39-day campaign shaped by the trade war
briefs.summary: Premier Christine Fréchette dissolved the legislature Thursday, setting an Oct. 5 vote in which the CAQ seeks a third mandate; one leader summed up the mood by calling Trump "my principal opponent."

briefs.headline: Ariane 6 lofts Europe's storm-watching satellite MTG-I2
briefs.summary: The rocket's first geostationary mission carried EUMETSAT's imager from French Guiana on Thursday; the satellite will scan Europe every 2.5 minutes for fast-developing severe storms, completing the first Meteosat Third Generation trio.

briefs.headline: A brain 'brake' shuts off chronic nerve pain in mice
briefs.summary: Washington University researchers report in Current Biology that mu opioid receptors in the locus coeruleus restrain pain circuits: deleting them made injured mice hypersensitive, and restoring them switched the pain back off.

briefs.headline: Hubble pins a dwarf-galaxy merger to the Milky Way's youth
briefs.summary: Ages and chemistry of 39 inner-galaxy globular clusters reveal a galaxy of some 500 million solar masses, named LKH, merging about 11.8 billion years ago — pushing the galaxy's known merger record back 1.8 billion years, per Nature Astronomy.

briefs.headline: AI finds six printer settings for a NASA rocket alloy
briefs.summary: A Washington State University model searched over 100 million laser configurations for printing copper alloy GRCop-42 and, in 40 experiments, found six that work — one at a record-low 500 watts, within reach of most commercial printers.

briefs.headline: Alberta faces water questions at AI data-centre town halls
briefs.summary: Premier Danielle Smith and Technology Minister Nate Glubish held the third of four virtual town halls Thursday on data-centre development, after earlier sessions drew demands for safeguards on environmental risk and water use.

art.caption: Rescuers walk residents across the mud-buried valley floor, past a house gutted to its frame.

weather_ear: Forecast at 7:15, from the weather desk.
kicker: Huntington, the Mid-Ohio Valley and Summers were quiet; Webster County's half of Vacation Hotspots came up empty.
